hook: Telangana villages to keep own revenue in *bank* accounts, not treasury
hook_b: Telangana villages to keep own revenue in *bank* accounts, not treasury
tldr: The Panchayat Raj Department told District Panchayat Officers to open zero-balance 'OSR Account' savings accounts for every gram panchayat.

beats.what: Accounts will be at designated SBI and Union Bank branches and used only for own-source revenue.
beats.why: The Telangana Panchayat Raj (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2026 changed Section 70(3), in force from Oct 9, 2026.
beats.care: Village taxes and fees will now sit in dedicated bank accounts managed by the panchayats.

cards.title: 🆕 What's new
cards.body: The Hindu: Commissioner Divya Devarajan directed DPOs to open 'OSR Account – [GP name]' accounts; Rangareddy, Sangareddy and Siddipet are among SBI districts.

cards.q: Should village councils control their own revenue directly?

qs: Who audits spending from the new OSR accounts?

facts.t: The Panchayat Raj (Fourth Amendment) Act, 2026 came into force on *October 9, 2026*.

learn.t: OSR = Own Source Revenue, money a panchayat raises itself (taxes, fees).

watch: Banks have been asked to open and configure accounts on priority; no deadline given.

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.title: Telangana directs Gram Panchayats to open separate bank accounts for own revenue

fact: Telangana gram panchayats must now bank their own revenue, *not* route it via treasury.
twist: SBI handles 15 districts and Union Bank 16 under the new zero-balance OSR accounts.
